77:{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_38","type":"command_execution","command":"/bin/bash -lc 'cat docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex'","aggregated_output":"\\documentclass[11pt]{article}\n\n\\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}\n\\usepackage{xurl}\n\\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}\n\\setlength{\\emergencystretch}{2em}\n\n\\input{command}\n\n\\title{Proof-Gap Protocol for Source-Faithful Formalization}\n\\author{}\n\\date{2026-05-11}\n\n\\begin{document}\n\\maketitle\n\n\\section{Purpose}\n\nThis note fixes terminology for a recurring failure mode in the formalization\nof the low individual degree test paper, \\path{arXiv:2009.12982}.  It\ncomplements the note-writing policy in \\path{docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex} and\nthe source-statement audit tracked historically in \\ghissue{1458}.  The current\nsource-boundary proof holes are tracked in \\ghissue{1507} and \\ghissue{422}.\nA proof may be blocked at\nan intermediate mathematical assertion.  If that assertion is added as a new\nhypothesis to a theorem labelled as a paper theorem, the resulting \\Lean{}\ntheorem\nmay be correct as a conditional statement, but it is no longer the theorem in\nthe cited source.  The apparent proof has not closed the paper theorem; it has\nmoved a proof obligation into the theorem statement.\n\nThe protocol below distinguishes such proof debt from legitimate formal\nboundary conditions and from genuine mathematical corrections.  It is meant for\ncontributors and reviewers who must decide whether a bridge, residual, repair,\ninput, or obligation structure is a proved local construction, a tracked proof\ngap, or statement drift which must be repaired before a theorem may be\nadvertised as a source theorem.  The default rule is restrictive: such data\nmust not be added to a paper-facing theorem unless it is part of the cited\nsource statement or a documented faithful encoding of its ambient hypotheses.\n\n\\section{Basic objects}\n\n\\paragraph{Source theorem.}\nA source theorem is a theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary in the paper\nsource under \\path{references/ldt-paper/}.  Its hypotheses and conclusion are\nthe mathematical ground truth, subject only to faithful formal encoding and to\ndocumented paper-gap corrections.\n\n\\paragraph{Paper-facing declaration.}\nA \\Lean{} declaration is paper-facing when it is named or cited as the\nformalization of a source theorem, for instance through a blueprint\n\\verb|\\lean{}| link on a theorem environment carrying a paper label.  Such a\ndeclaration must match the source theorem in its public statement.  In\nparticular, it may not add an unproved bridge, residual, repair, input,\nobligation structure, or other proof-obligation hypothesis which the paper does\nnot assume.\n\n\\paragraph{Proof obligation.}\nA proof obligation is an intermediate assertion needed by the proof of a source\ntheorem.  It may be a construction, an estimate, a transport lemma, or a\ncomparison between two formal representations.  If the paper proves or invokes\nthis assertion, then the formalization should state it as a separate lemma or\ntheorem and prove it from the upstream hypotheses.\n\n\\paragraph{Obligation discharger.}\nAn obligation discharger is a theorem or definition which constructs a proof\nobligation from the paper hypotheses already available at that point in the\nargument.  This is the preferred representation of missing work.  If the proof\nis not yet complete, the discharger may temporarily contain a tracked\n\\verb|sorry|, but the paper-facing theorem should call it rather than assume\nits output as an additional theorem hypothesis.\n\n\\paragraph{Conditional helper.}\nA conditional helper is a separately named theorem whose statement explicitly\nassumes a proof obligation.  Names such as\n\\leanid{mainFormal\\_ofInternalObligations},\n\\leanid{orthonormalization\\_ofInput}, or names whose suffix advertises the\nassumed obligation are permitted only when the declaration is not presented as\nthe source theorem.  A conditional helper is a quarantine for downstream proof\ncontent; it does not close the source theorem.\n\n\\section{Bridge, residual, repair, input, and obligation structures}\n\nThe words \\emph{bridge}, \\emph{residual}, \\emph{repair}, \\emph{input}, and\n\\emph{obligation structure} name possible formal shapes.  They become dangerous\nwhen their mathematical status is unclear or when their names make unproved\ndata look like acceptable hypotheses of a source theorem.\n\n\\paragraph{Bridge.}\nA bridge should be a transport theorem between two already defined\nmathematical forms: for example, a tensor-placement identity, a conversion\nbetween two equivalent consistency relations, or a statement translating a\nsource object into a formal representation.  A bridge is harmless only after it\nis proved from previously available assumptions.  It becomes proof debt when it\nis assumed because the transport has not yet been proved.  It becomes theorem\ndrift when the assumed bridge is added to a paper-facing theorem.\n\n\\paragraph{Residual.}\nA residual is a named remainder after part of an argument has been performed.\nIt is often a useful way to record the exact missing target after a completed\nconstruction.  A residual may appear as the conclusion of a helper theorem or\nas the input of a quarantined conditional helper.  It is not a permissible new\nassumption on a paper theorem unless the paper itself assumes that residual.\n\n\\paragraph{Input.}\nAn input is a named bundle of data or hypotheses consumed by a construction or\nconditional helper.  It is harmless only when each load-bearing field is either\npart of the source hypotheses or is produced by an earlier theorem.  It becomes\nproof debt when the bundle is merely assumed because the construction of its\nfields is missing.  It becomes theorem drift when such a bundle is added to the\npublic statement of a source theorem.\n\n\\paragraph{Repair.}\nA repair is a mathematical construction which replaces an approximate or\npartial object by a better object, usually with a quantitative estimate.  In\nthe low individual degree test formalization, projectivization and\northonormalization repairs are genuine mathematical operations.  A repair\nshould therefore appear as a construction or as a theorem discharging the\ncorresponding obligation.  If a theorem assumes the output of the repair instead\nof constructing it, that theorem is conditional on the repair.\n\n\\paragraph{Obligation structure.}\nAn obligation structure is a record whose fields are the data and estimates\nneeded by a later construction.  This is acceptable only as an internal target\nor as a hypothesis of a conditional helper.  Such a structure becomes statement\ndrift if it is added to a paper-facing theorem instead of being constructed\ninside the proof.  The review question is whether every load-bearing field is\nproved from the source hypotheses or is explicitly tracked as a missing\nobligation.\n\n\\section{The main failure mode}\n\nSuppose the paper proves\n\\[\n  H \\Longrightarrow C.\n\\]\nDuring formalization, the proof may need an intermediate assertion \\(B\\).  The\npaper theorem should be represented as\n\\[\n  H \\Longrightarrow B \\Longrightarrow C\n  \\quad\\text{inside the proof,}\n\\]\nwhere \\(B\\) is obtained by a lemma or theorem from \\(H\\).  The following\npublic statement is a different theorem:\n\\[\n  H \\land B \\Longrightarrow C.\n\\]\nIt is not unsound in \\Lean{}, but it is not the paper theorem.  It says that the\nconclusion follows if the missing bridge data is supplied.  Such a theorem is a\nconditional helper, even if its conclusion looks exactly like the paper's\nconclusion.\n\nThis is the situation colloquially described as ``adding a bridge\nhypothesis''.  More precisely, an unproved intermediate step has been promoted\nfrom the proof body to the theorem's assumptions.  The correction is not to hide\nthe hypothesis under a different structure name.  The correction is to keep a\npaper-facing theorem with the source statement and move the missing step to a\nnamed internal proof obligation.\n\n\\section{Faithful boundary hypotheses}\n\nNot every extra formal hypothesis is a theorem drift.  Some hypotheses are\nfaithful boundary conditions introduced by formal encoding.  Examples include\nnonnegativity needed for a real power, positivity needed to divide by a\nquantity, finiteness and nonemptiness of an index type, a field-model instance,\nor decidability instances required by \\Lean{}.  Such hypotheses are acceptable\nwhen they express part of the mathematical ambient setting or make explicit a\ncondition used implicitly in the paper.\n\nThe distinction is load-bearing.  A faithful boundary hypothesis describes the\ndomain in which the paper's objects live.  A proof-debt hypothesis supplies a\nmathematical step that the proof should derive.  If removing the hypothesis\nleaves an unproved construction or estimate from the paper proof, then the\nhypothesis is proof debt, not a boundary condition.\n\n\\section{Definition drift and subtree repair}\n\nDefinition drift is especially dangerous because it propagates.  If a\ndefinition is changed so that it no longer denotes the object in the paper,\nthen every downstream theorem using that definition may continue to compile\nwhile proving statements about the wrong object.  Downstream theorem statements\ncan then be repaired piecemeal, but the development remains unstable because\nthe wrong definition is still upstream.\n\nWhen a definition mismatch is found, the repair should proceed by a subtree\nprotocol.\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item Identify the source object and the formal object precisely.\n  \\item Freeze a source-faithful definition or state an adapter theorem\n  relating the existing definition to the source object.\n  \\item Recheck the downstream theorem chain against that definition or adapter.\n  \\item Re-formalize the affected subtree from the corrected interface, rather\n  than adding local hypotheses to each downstream theorem.\n  \\item If a downstream proof cannot be completed, record the missing obligation\n  at the lowest point where the paper proof needs it.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nThis is slower than editing a final theorem signature, but it prevents a local\ndefinition error from becoming a global theorem-statement error.\n\n\\section{Allowed shapes}\n\n\\begin{center}\n\\begin{tabular}{p{0.24\\linewidth}p{0.31\\linewidth}p{0.32\\linewidth}}\n\\textbf{Shape} & \\textbf{Allowed use} & \\textbf{Forbidden use} \\\\\n\\hline\nPaper-facing theorem & Matches the source statement up to faithful encoding &\nCarries non-paper bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, or\nproof-obligation hypotheses \\\\\nSource-shaped theorem with a tracked \\verb|sorry| & Default repair when the\nsource proof is blocked but the statement is known & Replaced by a strengthened\ntheorem statement merely to keep the file compiling \\\\\nConditional helper & Temporary quarantine for substantial proof content whose\nremaining named obligation has not yet been discharged & Introduced merely to\navoid a \\verb|sorry|, or linked as the source theorem or marked as\nproof-complete for that theorem \\\\\nObligation discharger theorem & Constructs the obligation from paper hypotheses &\nMerely restates the obligation as an assumption \\\\\nInput bundle & Collects produced data for a local construction & Is assumed by a\nsource theorem instead of being produced \\\\\nObligation structure & Bundles constructed data and estimates & Hides unproved\nfields that are then assumed by a source theorem \\\\\nPaper-gap note & Documents a real mathematical or formal-statement divergence &\nJustifies silent statement drift without a repair plan\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{center}\n\n\\section{Protocol for a blocked proof}\n\nWhen a source-labelled proof is blocked, use the following order.\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item Read the cited source statement and the proof passage in\n  \\path{references/ldt-paper/}.\n  \\item Write the paper theorem form, the current \\Lean{} theorem form, and the\n  first missing intermediate assertion.\n  \\item Decide whether the missing assertion is a faithful boundary condition,\n  a representation adapter, an ordinary lemma from the paper proof, or a real\n  paper-gap discrepancy.\n  \\item If it is an ordinary lemma or adapter, create a named theorem which\n  discharges that obligation.  Do not add it to the source theorem as a new\n  hypothesis.\n  \\item Keep the source-labelled theorem itself in the source form, even if its\n  proof must contain a tracked \\verb|sorry|.  This is the default repair when\n  the missing assertion has not yet been proved.\n  \\item Create a conditional helper only to quarantine substantial proof content\n  that already exists and would otherwise be lost.  Do not create such a helper\n  merely to avoid a \\verb|sorry| or to keep making progress.  If a conditional\n  helper remains, give it a conditional name, keep it separate from the\n  paper-facing theorem, and record the obligation discharger that must eliminate\n  it.\n  \\item If the source and formal statements genuinely differ, write or update a\n  note under \\path{docs/paper-gaps/} before marking the statement as aligned.\n  \\item Update the blueprint so that paper labels point only to paper-facing\n  declarations.  Conditional helpers belong in remarks or implementation\n  notes, not in the source theorem block.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\\section{Retirement criterion}\n\nAn auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or\nrenamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all three of the\nfollowing conditions hold:\n\\begin{enumerate}\n  \\item it is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited\n        outside result;\n  \\item no current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated;\n  \\item it assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data,\n        repair data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper\n        proof requires.\n\\end{enumerate}\nIf such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, it\nshould remain a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.\nIt should not be a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should\nnot support a source-labelled blueprint \\verb|\\leanok| claim.\n\n\\section{Review questions}\n\nA reviewer should first compare every paper-labelled declaration with the cited\nsource statement, checking both hypotheses and conclusion up to faithful formal\nencoding.  Bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, and\nproof-obligation assumptions should be absent from paper-facing theorem\nsignatures unless they occur in the paper.  If a conditional helper remains,\nits name should be explicitly conditional and it should not support a source\ntheorem \\verb|\\leanok| claim.\nEach load-bearing obligation-structure or input field should have a theorem\ndischarging it, a tracked issue, or an explicit \\verb|sorry| at the obligation\nsite.  When a definition has changed, the downstream subtree should be checked\nagainst the corrected definition rather than patched locally.  Finally, if the\nformal statement genuinely differs from the source statement, a paper-gap note\nshould explain the mathematical difference and give a plan to remove or justify\nit.\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\nThe project should prefer visible proof obligations over invisible statement\ndrift.  A tracked \\verb|sorry| in the source-shaped theorem, or in the lowest\nnamed internal obligation needed by its proof, is less misleading than a source\ntheorem whose assumptions have been strengthened.  Conditional helpers are not a\nnormal substitute for unfinished proofs; they are temporary quarantines for\nsubstantial proof content, and they must remain conditional until the missing\nobligation is discharged.  The paper-facing declaration is reserved for the\ntheorem proved by the paper, or for a documented corrected version whose\nmathematical difference is explicit.\n\n\\end{document}\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

This module computes the two source blocks of the direction of an extended
diagonal line.  That direction is obtained from an unrestricted extended

the `i`-th coordinate of a block, that block inherits the truncation at `i`,
the preceding block is retained untruncated, and every later block vanishes.
The computation is recorded after transport to the source scalar field, since
the extended direction and the source line directions are presented over the
two identified scalar fields.

The block computations support `lem:qld-sublines` in
blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.

`def:ld-question-distribution`; the coordinate blocks are those of
blueprint `def:combine-map`.

    (hi : i.val = 0) (v : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :
    prefixProjection i v = v := by
  funext j
  simp [prefixProjection, hi]

/-!
# Coordinate blocks of a truncated extended direction

This module computes the two source blocks of the direction of an extended
diagonal line.  That direction is obtained from an unrestricted extended
vector by zeroing the coordinates that precede the stored coordinate index,
so each source block is again a prefix truncation: when the stored index is
the `i`-th coordinate of a block, that block inherits the truncation at `i`,

>>>>>>> 37f9d1acb03d14288c171784447145e16f8a3b61
The computation is recorded after transport to the source scalar field, since
the extended direction and the source line directions are presented over the
two identified scalar fields.

## References

The block computations support `lem:qld-sublines` in
blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
The truncation is the prefix restriction of blueprint
`def:ld-question-distribution`; the coordinate blocks are those of
blueprint `def:combine-map`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-! ## Truncation at the first coordinate -/

/-- Zeroing the coordinates preceding the first coordinate changes nothing.
Blueprint `def:ld-question-distribution`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
theorem prefixProjection_of_val_zero {L : LdParams} {i : Fin L.m}
    (hi : i.val = 0) (v : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :
    prefixProjection i v = v := by
  funext j
  simp [prefixProjection, hi]

/-! ## The `X` block of a truncated extended direction -/

/-- The `X` block of an extended direction truncated at an `X`-block
coordinate is the `X` block truncated at that coordinate of the source space.
Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem projX_directPrefixProjection_embX (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m)
    (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    projX (directPointToPauli P
        (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embX P.m i) v)) =
      prefixProjection (P := P.toLdParams) i (projX (directPointToPauli P v)) := by
  funext a
  change extendedDirectScalarEquiv P
      (if (embX P.m a).val < (embX P.m i).val then 0 else v (embX P.m a)) =
    if a.val < i.val then 0 else extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (v (embX P.m a))
  rw [embX_val, embX_val]
  by_cases h : a.val < i.val
  · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h, map_zero]
  · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h]

/-- The `X` block of an extended direction truncated at a `Z`-block
coordinate vanishes.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem projX_directPrefixProjection_embZ (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m)
    (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    projX (directPointToPauli P
      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embZ P.m i) v)) = 0 := by
  funext a
  have ha : a.val < P.m := a.isLt
  change extendedDirectScalarEquiv P
      (if (embX P.m a).val < (embZ P.m i).val then 0 else v (embX P.m a)) =
    (0 : PauliScalar P)
  rw [embX_val, embZ_val, if_pos (by omega), map_zero]

/-- The `X` block of an extended direction truncated at the first scalar
coordinate vanishes.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem projX_directPrefixProjection_alphaVar (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    projX (directPointToPauli P
      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (alphaVar P.m) v)) = 0 := by
  funext a
  have ha : a.val < P.m := a.isLt
  change extendedDirectScalarEquiv P
      (if (embX P.m a).val < (alphaVar P.m).val then 0 else v (embX P.m a)) =
    (0 : PauliScalar P)
  rw [embX_val, alphaVar_val, if_pos (by omega), map_zero]

/-- The `X` block of an extended direction truncated at the second scalar
coordinate vanishes.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem projX_directPrefixProjection_betaVar (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    projX (directPointToPauli P
      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (betaVar P.m) v)) = 0 := by
  funext a
  have ha : a.val < P.m := a.isLt
  change extendedDirectScalarEquiv P
      (if (embX P.m a).val < (betaVar P.m).val then 0 else v (embX P.m a)) =
    (0 : PauliScalar P)
  rw [embX_val, betaVar_val, if_pos (by omega), map_zero]

/-! ## The `Z` block of a truncated extended direction -/

/-- The `Z` block of an extended direction truncated at a `Z`-block
coordinate is the `Z` block truncated at that coordinate of the source space.
Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem projZ_directPrefixProjection_embZ (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m)
    (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    projZ (directPointToPauli P
        (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embZ P.m i) v)) =
      prefixProjection (P := P.toLdParams) i (projZ (directPointToPauli P v)) := by

    if a.val < i.val then 0 else extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (v (embZ P.m a))
  rw [embZ_val, embZ_val]
  by_cases h : a.val < i.val
  · rw [if_pos (by omega), if_pos h, map_zero]
  · rw [if_neg (by omega), if_neg h]

/-- The `Z` block of an extended direction truncated at an `X`-block
coordinate is the untruncated `Z` block, since every `Z`-block coordinate
follows every `X`-block coordinate.  Blueprint
`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem projZ_directPrefixProjection_embX (P : AdmissibleParams) (i : Fin P.m)
    (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    projZ (directPointToPauli P
        (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (embX P.m i) v)) =
      projZ (directPointToPauli P v) := by
  funext a
  have hi : i.val < P.m := i.isLt
  change extendedDirectScalarEquiv P
      (if (embZ P.m a).val < (embX P.m i).val then 0 else v (embZ P.m a)) =
    extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (v (embZ P.m a))
  rw [embZ_val, embX_val, if_neg (by omega)]

/-- The `Z` block of an extended direction truncated at the first scalar
coordinate vanishes.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem projZ_directPrefixProjection_alphaVar (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    projZ (directPointToPauli P
      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (alphaVar P.m) v)) = 0 := by
  funext a
  have ha : a.val < P.m := a.isLt

      (if (embZ P.m a).val < (alphaVar P.m).val then 0 else v (embZ P.m a)) =
    (0 : PauliScalar P)
  rw [embZ_val, alphaVar_val, if_pos (by omega), map_zero]

/-- The `Z` block of an extended direction truncated at the second scalar
coordinate vanishes.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
theorem projZ_directPrefixProjection_betaVar (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (v : Fin P.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    projZ (directPointToPauli P
      (directPrefixProjection (D := P.extendedDirectLd) (betaVar P.m) v)) = 0 := by
  funext a
  have ha : a.val < P.m := a.isLt

  rw [embZ_val, betaVar_val, if_pos (by omega), map_zero]

end

# Resolve `current` exactly ONCE to a concrete snapshot path.  The warmer
# publishes by rename, so a single readlink always yields a whole, immutable tree;
# re-resolving mid-run could straddle a publish.
resolve_snapshot() {
  [ -L "$CURRENT_LINK" ] || return 1
  local target
  target="$(readlink "$CURRENT_LINK")" || return 1
  [ -n "$target" ] || return 1
  [ -d "$target/build" ] || return 1
  [ -f "$target/STAMP" ] || return 1
  printf '%s' "$target"

stamp_field() { # <stamp-file> <key>
  local file="$1" key="$2" line value
  [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    case "$line" in
      "$key="*)
        value="${line#*=}"
        # The STAMP is on-disk data: validate, never eval or source it.
        case "$key" in
          keyhash)
            [ "${#value}" -eq 64 ] || return 1
            case "$value" in *[!0-9a-f]*) return 1 ;; esac
            ;;
          sha)
            case "$value" in ''|*[!0-9a-f]*) return 1 ;; esac
            ;;

            case "$value" in complete|partial) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac

cow_copy() { # <src-dir> <dst-dir>

# exactly that fresh state.
proofwidgets_fresh_state_workaround() { # <tree>
  local tree="$1" pkg name

  # inside a vendored package: it would delete downloaded build output and cost

  for pkg in "$tree"/.lake/packages/*; do

run_outside_git_env() (
  if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    for name in $(git rev-parse --local-env-vars); do
      unset "$name" || true
    done
  fi
  "$@"
)

sha256_stdin() {
  if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    shasum -a 256 | awk '{print $1}'
  elif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    sha256sum | awk '{print $1}'
}

cleanup() {
  local rc=$?
  if [ -n "$INCOMING_DIR" ] && [ -d "$INCOMING_DIR" ]; then
    rm -rf "$INCOMING_DIR"
  fi
  release_full_build_lock
  exit "$rc"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- telemetry

resolve_primary_repo() {
  local common root
  if common="$(run_outside_git_env git -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)" \
     && [ -n "$common" ]; then
    root="$(dirname "$common")"
    if [ -d "$root/local/bin" ]; then
      printf '%s' "$root"
      return 0
    fi
  fi
  ( cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd )
}

append_build_telemetry() { # <kind> <outcome> <seconds> <trigger> <sha> <note>
  local dir file waited=0
  dir="${MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR:-$(resolve_primary_repo)/results/telemetry}"
  file="$dir/builds.jsonl"
  if ! mkdir -p "$dir" 2>/dev/null; then
    warn "cannot create the telemetry directory $dir; build record dropped"
    return 0
  fi
  while ! mkdir "$TELEMETRY_LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
    if [ "$waited" -ge 5 ]; then
      warn "telemetry lock busy; appending without serialization"
      break
    fi
    sleep 1
    waited=$((waited + 1))
  done
  if ! python3 - "$file" "$(iso_now)" "$@" <<'PY'
import json
import sys

path, ts, kind, outcome, seconds, trigger, sha, note = sys.argv[1:9]


def clean(text, limit=400):
    return "".join(c for c in text if c == " " or c.isprintable())[:limit]


record = {
    "ts": ts,
    "kind": clean(kind, 32),
    "trigger": clean(trigger, 200),
    "outcome": clean(outcome, 32),
}
try:
    record["seconds"] = int(float(seconds))
except (TypeError, ValueError):
    record["seconds"] = None
if sha:
    record["sha"] = clean(sha, 64)
if note:
    record["note"] = clean(note)
with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    handle.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
PY
  then
    warn "failed to append build telemetry to $file"
  fi
  rmdir "$TELEMETRY_LOCK" 2>/dev/null || true
}
